title: SEBI's 2026 overlap limits within fund houses
objectives: State SEBI's February 2026 overlap rules, how they are measured, and the compliance window.
Say why a client's own portfolio still needs checking.
body_md:
SEBI's circular of 26 February 2026 on categorisation and rationalisation of schemes: value and contra funds — an AMC may offer both only if their portfolio overlap is no more than 50%. Sectoral and thematic funds — no more than 50% overlap with the AMC's other equity schemes (large-cap schemes excepted). How it is measured: quarterly, using the average of daily overlap values. Time to comply: existing sectoral/thematic schemes have 3 years; those still breaching must be merged. Disclosure: AMCs disclose category-wise overlap levels on their websites every month.

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Value and contra funds | An AMC may offer both only if their portfolio overlap is no more than 50% |
| Sectoral and thematic funds | No more than 50% overlap with the AMC's other equity schemes (large-cap schemes excepted) |
| How it is measured | Quarterly, using the average of daily overlap values |
| Time to comply | Existing sectoral/thematic schemes have 3 years; those still breaching must be merged |
| Disclosure | AMCs disclose category-wise overlap levels on their websites every month |

These rules apply within one fund house. A client holding funds from different AMCs can still have high overlap, so checking the client's own portfolio remains our job.
example: An AMC's sectoral fund at 60% overlap with its other equity schemes: it has 3 years to come within 50%, or be merged.
say: SEBI's limits apply within one fund house.
A client across AMCs can still have high overlap.
never: SEBI's limits prevent all client overlap.
Sectoral funds have no overlap limit.

check.q: Under SEBI’s February 2026 circular, an AMC’s value and contra funds may overlap by no more than…
check.why: 50%. Both can be offered only within this limit.

check.q: The 50% overlap cap with other equity schemes applies to…
check.why: Sectoral and thematic schemes. Large-cap schemes are excepted from the comparison.

check.q: Do SEBI’s overlap limits prevent overlap across different AMCs?
o: No, they apply within one AMC
check.why: No, they apply within one AMC. We still need to check the client’s portfolio.
